questions.question: A customer reports intermittent packet loss during peak. As NDM, which response best shows Customer Obsession?
options: Prioritize restoring customer impact, communicate status clearly, and drive durable fixes beyond a temporary workaround
Avoid customers and focus only on internal tickets
Wait for perfect information before any action
Delegate all technical judgment permanently to vendors

questions.question: For Amazon LP interviews, STAR stands for:
options: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Scope, Team, Agenda, Report
Strategy, Timeline, Analysis, Review
Summary, Test, Automate, Release
questions.explanation: Structure answers so Actions are yours and Results are quantified.

questions.question: Amazon LP answers should emphasize "I" for:
options: Your specific decisions and actions, with "we" only for shared context
Everything the company did
Never using I — only we
Only the Result section
questions.explanation: Bar Raisers need to score your individual contribution.

questions.question: A weak Result statement is:
options: "Things got better and the team was happy"
"P99 loss dropped from 0.8% to 0.05% over 6 weeks"
"MTTR fell from 90m to 25m after runbook automation"
"Change failure rate fell 40% quarter-over-quarter"
questions.explanation: Quantify impact. Vague happiness is not Deliver Results.

questions.question: Bar Raisers often probe failure stories. Strongest pattern:
options: Honest miss, your role, systemic fix, and what you do differently now
Blame another team entirely
Claim you have never failed
Hide the failure and invent a success
questions.explanation: Learn and Be Curious / Earn Trust reward ownership of misses.
